text: The recent laboratory results show that your Creatine Kinase, Aldolase, and thyroid function are all within normal limits, which makes inflammatory myopathies and thyroid disease unlikely. Given the persistent combination of vertical double vision and proximal limb weakness that worsens with activity, do you have any history of eating disorders or significant weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1.

The combination of distal and proximal weakness, ptosis/diplopia, and the absence of inflammatory markers or sensory deficits is highly characteristic of this condition. Given that we have already used 9 of your 10 allowed questions, I will conclude here.
